final_answer: All eight decision atoms (DA-001 through DA-008) reached A/B/C consensus, drew no conflicts, and were graded 'accept' by the judge with totals ranging 0.84–0.915. The micro-debate was skipped because there was nothing in dispute. Therefore the final record ACCEPTS every atom and REJECTS none. The agreed design: implement TelegramReporter in src/oko/live/reporters.py against the existing Reporter ABC's report(payload: BridgeOutput); send only when payload.description is non-empty (the VLM/human-animal indicator); format the message exactly as '👁 ОКО: <description>'; read the bot token from ~/.bridge-private/secrets.json (telegramBotToken) via the existing secrets loader; inject an HTTP transport for offline tests; flip service.py's default config_path to configs/live-webcam.yaml; keep the reporter OFF by default and only register it via build_reporter_from_env() when OKO_TG_CHAT (or config chat_id) AND a token are present; and add focused pytest cases. The one cross-atom resolution folded in: DA-008 originally referenced a private '_http_post' mock target while DA-005 mandates an injectable transport seam — the tests MUST mock the injected transport object (e.g. a post(url, json) callable), not a private method, so assertions match the actual DI seam. Before committing, the implementation must verify the real ABC signature, the secrets-loader API/field name, the transport interface shape, and the existence of configs/live-webcam.yaml — these are the only residual unknowns the judge flagged.

decisions.decision: DA-001: Implement TelegramReporter in src/oko/live/reporters.py, implementing the existing Reporter ABC's report(self, payload: BridgeOutput) method.
decisions.rationale: A+B consensus and the foundational atom — everything else depends on it. Building against the existing Reporter contract is the low-surprise architectural fit and maximizes reuse of the reporter dispatch pipeline. Judge total 0.8775.
alternatives_considered: Standalone notifier module/script that does not implement the Reporter interface (rejected: bypasses existing dispatch and reduces reuse)
Introducing a new reporter interface (rejected: unnecessary churn; the existing ABC already fits)
decisions.risk: Assumes the Reporter ABC and the exact report(payload: BridgeOutput) signature exist as stated; must be verified against the actual interface before final commit.
decisions.test: Confirm the TelegramReporter class lives in src/oko/live/reporters.py and correctly implements the report method of the Reporter ABC.

decisions.decision: DA-002: Gate sending on a non-empty payload.description — emit a Telegram message only for VLM-described (human/animal) events.
decisions.rationale: Full A+B+C consensus. A trivial, high-value guard that prevents noisy object-only events from spamming Telegram; cheap, reversible, and directly reduces operational risk. Judge total 0.915 (highest in set).
alternatives_considered: Check an explicit event-type/kind flag instead of description presence (viable but adds coupling; description-non-empty is the canonical VLM signal in the stated design)
Send all events and filter on the Telegram side (rejected: spammy, wasteful API calls)
decisions.risk: Relies on non-empty description being the canonical VLM indicator; sound given the stated design but confirm no VLM event can legitimately have an empty description.
decisions.test: Pass a BridgeOutput with an empty description to the reporter and assert that no Telegram API call is made.

decisions.decision: DA-003: Format the message text strictly as '👁 ОКО: <description>' using the VLM description.
decisions.rationale: A+B consensus on the exact template. Highly specific and trivial to implement and assert; the precise string makes DA-008's assertion unambiguous. Judge total 0.8525.
alternatives_considered: Richer multi-line message with timestamp/metadata (rejected: out of scope; contract mandates this exact format)
decisions.risk: Cosmetic only; low risk. Ensure the emoji and Cyrillic text are emitted as UTF-8 without mangling.
decisions.test: Assert the text field in the sendMessage request body equals f'👁 ОКО: {payload.description}' for a VLM event.

decisions.decision: DA-004: Read the bot token from the telegramBotToken field in ~/.bridge-private/secrets.json, reusing the existing secrets-loading pattern.
decisions.rationale: A+B+C consensus. Reuse-driven and keeps credentials out of the repo. Reusing the established loader mitigates inherent secrets-handling risk. Judge total 0.85.
alternatives_considered: Read token directly from an environment variable (rejected: contract specifies the secrets file)
Bespoke JSON parsing instead of the shared loader (rejected: duplicates logic and diverges from existing patterns)
decisions.risk: Secrets handling carries inherent risk; must confirm the exact existing loader API and the precise field name during implementation.
decisions.test: Unit test mocking ~/.bridge-private/secrets.json that verifies the reporter loads telegramBotToken correctly.

decisions.decision: DA-005: Accept an injectable HTTP transport parameter for requests, enabling fully offline unit tests.
decisions.rationale: A+B+C consensus. A clean dependency-injection seam yielding deterministic, network-free tests. Strong risk-reduction and feasibility. Judge total 0.8675.
alternatives_considered: Monkeypatching the HTTP client at module level in tests (rejected: brittle, less explicit than DI)
Mocking a private _http_post method (rejected per cross-atom resolution: the public injected transport is the canonical seam)
decisions.risk: Exact transport interface must be pinned (e.g., a post(url, json=...) callable returning a response); default to the project's HTTP client when none injected.
decisions.test: Inject a mock transport and verify the reporter calls its post method with the correct sendMessage URL and JSON payload.

decisions.decision: DA-006: Change the default config_path in service.py/Settings to configs/live-webcam.yaml.
decisions.rationale: A+B+C consensus. One-line, highly reversible convenience change that makes the service work on a webcam out of the box. Judge total 0.84.
alternatives_considered: Keep example.yaml as default and require explicit override (rejected: fails the out-of-the-box webcam goal)
decisions.risk: Changing a global default can alter behavior for callers relying on the prior default, and assumes the target YAML exists; verify configs/live-webcam.yaml is present and that no existing flow depends on the old default before committing.
decisions.test: Unit test asserting Settings().config_path (or equivalent) defaults to 'configs/live-webcam.yaml'.

decisions.decision: DA-007: Keep TelegramReporter disabled by default; conditionally register it (preferably via build_reporter_from_env()) only when a chat_id (OKO_TG_CHAT or config) AND a token are present.
decisions.rationale: A+B+C consensus. Fail-safe wiring that prevents accidental sends — high risk-reduction. Routing through the existing factory maximizes reuse. Judge total 0.8525.
alternatives_considered: Always instantiate the reporter and no-op internally when unconfigured (rejected: less explicit, risks accidental sends if a token leaks in)
Enable purely from config file with no env override (rejected: contract mandates OKO_TG_CHAT support)
decisions.risk: Adds wiring/branching; 'preferably via build_reporter_from_env()' leaves a small wiring-location choice open — confirm the factory exists and is the right insertion point, else wire in service initialization.
decisions.test: Test build_reporter_from_env()/service init: TelegramReporter is added when OKO_TG_CHAT is set and a token is available, and absent otherwise.

decisions.decision: DA-008: Add focused pytest cases — VLM event posts correct text + chat_id via the injected transport; object-only (empty description) event posts zero times; Settings.config_path default equals configs/live-webcam.yaml.
decisions.rationale: A+B consensus. These cases lock in DA-002/003/005/006/007 and provide the strongest risk-reduction in the set; highly specific and feasible given the DI seam. Judge total 0.875.
alternatives_considered: Integration test hitting the real Telegram API (rejected: non-deterministic, requires network and live token)
Mocking a private _http_post (superseded by the cross-atom resolution to mock the injected transport)
decisions.risk: Mock target must align with the DI seam from DA-005 (the injected transport object), not a private _http_post, so assertions match the implementation.
decisions.test: 1) Inject mock transport; assert a VLM event triggers a POST to api.telegram.org/.../sendMessage with text '👁 ОКО: <description>' and the configured chat_id. 2) Assert an object-only (empty description) event triggers zero transport calls. 3) Assert Settings().config_path == 'configs/live-webcam.yaml'.

open_questions: Does the existing Reporter ABC expose exactly report(self, payload: BridgeOutput), and does BridgeOutput carry a `description` field populated by the Gemini VLM step? (DA-001/DA-002 verification)
What is the exact existing secrets-loader API and does the secrets.json field name match 'telegramBotToken' precisely? (DA-004)
What is the concrete injectable transport interface — a callable post(url, json=...) returning a response, or a client object — and what is the default transport when none is injected? (DA-005)
Does configs/live-webcam.yaml exist and is there any existing caller that relies on the previous default config_path (example.yaml)? (DA-006)
Does build_reporter_from_env() already exist as the reporter factory, or should the conditional wiring live in service.py initialization instead? (DA-007)

Should send failures (network errors / non-200 Telegram responses) be swallowed-and-logged so a Telegram outage never breaks the event pipeline? (implied operational concern, not explicitly in any atom)
implementation_plan: Step 0 (verify prerequisites): Inspect src/oko/live/reporters.py and the Reporter ABC to confirm the report(payload: BridgeOutput) signature; confirm BridgeOutput.description; locate the existing secrets loader and the telegramBotToken field; locate build_reporter_from_env()/service.py wiring and the Settings.config_path default; confirm configs/live-webcam.yaml exists.

Step 1 (DA-001/DA-003/DA-005): Implement TelegramReporter(Reporter) in src/oko/live/reporters.py with a constructor taking token, chat_id, and an injectable transport (defaulting to the project HTTP client). Implement report() to build text f'👁 ОКО: {payload.description}' and POST to https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendMessage with {chat_id, text} via the transport.
Step 2 (DA-002): In report(), guard early-return when payload.description is empty/None so only VLM (human/animal) events are sent.
Step 3 (DA-004): Load telegramBotToken from ~/.bridge-private/secrets.json using the existing secrets-loading helper.

Step 4 (DA-007): In build_reporter_from_env() (or service init), read OKO_TG_CHAT (and/or config chat_id); only when both a chat_id and a token are available, instantiate and append TelegramReporter to the active reporters list — otherwise omit it (OFF by default).
Step 5 (DA-006): Change the default config_path in service.py/Settings from example.yaml to configs/live-webcam.yaml.

Step 6 (DA-008): Add pytest tests in tests/ using a mock injected transport: (a) VLM event posts to sendMessage with exact text and configured chat_id; (b) object-only/empty-description event makes zero transport calls; (c) Settings().config_path defaults to configs/live-webcam.yaml; plus a test that TelegramReporter is wired only when OKO_TG_CHAT + token are present.
Step 7: Run pytest and confirm green; fix any drift between the chosen transport seam and the test mock target.
next_step: Verify the actual contracts in the codebase first — the Reporter ABC / report(payload: BridgeOutput) signature and BridgeOutput.description, the secrets loader and telegramBotToken field, build_reporter_from_env(), and the presence of configs/live-webcam.yaml — since these are the only residual unknowns flagged by the judge; then implement DA-001.

red_team_findings.what: The `vlm_only` gate (`report()` returns unless `payload.description` is non-empty) does NOT restrict alerts to VLM/human-animal events. In this codebase `BridgeOutput.description` is populated from `event.description` (contract.py:44), which `builder.py` sets to a non-empty human-readable string for EVERY event — `'car entered zone'`, `'person moving'`, `'Motion detected'`, `'Camera feed is offline'`. Gemini text only OVERWRITES it when the VLM actually runs (live.py:258-259). Therefore object-only / track / motion / camera-offline events all arrive with non-empty descriptions, and `service.py` reports every `result.bridge_output`. At runtime the service will DM the user `👁 ОКО: car entered zone`, `👁 ОКО: Motion detected`, etc.
red_team_findings.why: Directly violates the contract's central constraint ('Alerts ONLY for events with VLM descriptions (human/animal)') and success_test #5/#10. Worse, it is a FALSE GREEN: the proposed unit test fabricates an 'object-only event' with empty `description` (via `_sample_output()` default `description=''`) — a state the real pipeline never produces — so the suite passes while the deployed behavior spams the user. The gate must key off whether the VLM actually produced text (e.g. a dedicated flag / the VlmOutcome), not off `description` non-emptiness, which is the wrong signal.

red_team_findings.what: Even for genuine person/animal events, the gate emits the WRONG text whenever the VLM did not run for that specific reported event: on debounce cooldown (live.py:124-125 skips the VLM block, leaving `description` = base `'person entered room'`) or on VLM provider failure (gate.py:128-129 sets `response=None`, so description is never overwritten). In those cases `vlm_only` mode still fires `👁 ОКО: person entered room` — the base builder string, not the gemini description.
red_team_findings.why: Violates the format/content intent of constraint «👁 ОКО: <описание>» where <описание> must be the gemini description. Repeated person events during the VLM cooldown window will each leak a non-gemini, mislabeled 'VLM' alert. This survives even if the gate were re-keyed to event_type, because the description field itself is not a reliable carrier of 'gemini ran for THIS payload'.

red_team_findings.what: DA-006's claim that flipping `Settings.config_path` to `configs/live-webcam.yaml` makes the service 'work on the webcam out of the box' is only validated by a `Path(...).is_file()` unit assertion. The real `main()` path runs `LiveReadinessChecker` (service.py:319-325) against a config that requires `models/yolo11m.pt` (a real file dependency), a `provider: webcam` device at index 0, and `GEMINI_API_KEY` (live-webcam.yaml:1-23). On any host missing any of these, readiness blocks → `FatalError` → exit 1.
red_team_findings.why: The green unit test does not exercise the contract's actual runtime promise (success_test #10). 'Out of the box' is true only on a fully-provisioned host; on a fresh checkout/CI/dev machine without the YOLO weights or an API key the service now fails to start where the old `fake-live.yaml` default started cleanly. The decision flags this in open_questions but proceeds as if the unit assertion proves the runtime behavior — it doesn't.

red_team_findings.what: DA-007 sets `vlm_only=True` only 'when chat_id resolves from the OKO_TG_CHAT path', but the implementation_plan collapses the resolution to a single `chat_id = os.getenv('OKO_TG_CHAT') or os.getenv('OKO_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID')`, which discards which variable supplied it. If implemented naively the env-built reporter becomes either always-`vlm_only` (regressing existing `OKO_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` users from rich text + keyframe/incident-video alerts to a bare one-line message) or never-`vlm_only` (the new OKO_TG_CHAT feature silently ships disabled).
red_team_findings.why: The existing test `test_build_reporter_from_env_telegram` only asserts `only_alerts is True` and never checks message format or `vlm_only`, so this behavioral regression for legacy users would pass green and ship undetected. The two env vars need to be tracked separately, not OR-folded, to preserve both behaviors — a subtlety the plan glosses over.
